_meta.description: Kubernetes removed/deprecated built-in API catalog for the EAC Upgrade Breakage Radar. Single verified source of truth for both the live inventory-scan path (catalogRules, consumed by DeprecationCatalog/UpgradeBreakageAnalyzer) and the pre-apply CrossGuard gate (detectorTable, consumed by DeprecatedApiDetector).
_meta.rowShapeNotes: catalogRules entries carry ruleId/title/remediation (one finding identity per GVK). detectorTable entries are lighter (deprecatedIn/removedIn/replacement only) and support a kind=="*" wildcard that matches any Kind under that apiVersion — this mirrors the original DeprecatedApiDetector.TABLE lookup (exact apiVersion+kind first, then apiVersion+"*").
_meta.regressionNote: catalogRules[0..49] and detectorTable[0..26] are verbatim, mechanically extracted copies of the pre-refactor DeprecationCatalog.java / DeprecatedApiDetector.java hardcoded tables (see scripts/fetch-deprecations.sh extraction step in the Phase-1 backend summary) — including two known, pre-existing, UNRECONCILED drifts between the two legacy tables for the flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1beta1 and v1beta2 groups (catalogRules has explicit FlowSchema/PriorityLevelConfiguration rows with different deprecatedIn than detectorTable's wildcard row for the same apiVersion). These are preserved AS-IS (not fixed) to guarantee byte-for-byte-unchanged behavior for both existing consumers; reconciling them is a deliberate follow-up, not part of this phase.

unconfirmedRemovals.verdict: RESOLVED 2026-08-28 — removedIn CORRECTED 1.36 -> 1.38 (and deprecatedIn 1.33 -> 1.35) in both catalogRules and detectorTable; provisional cleared. The earlier pass looked only at CHANGELOG prose and the (stale) website deprecation guide, neither of which carries the value. The kubernetes/kubernetes SOURCE TREE does.
unconfirmedRemovals.note: The 1.36 value came from CHANGELOG-1.33.md: 'The resource.k8s.io/v1beta1 API is deprecated and will be removed in 1.36. Use v1beta2 instead.' (#129970) — a forward-looking announcement upstream did not honour, which is why no later CHANGELOG confirms the removal. Authoritative value, read from kubernetes/kubernetes @ v1.38.0-alpha.0: staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1beta1/zz_generated.prerelease-lifecycle.go declares APILifecycleDeprecated()=1.35 and APILifecycleRemoved()=1.38 for all four kinds; pkg/controlplane/instance.go still lists resourcev1beta1 in betaAPIGroupVersionsDisabledByDefault (still served, disabled by default) at 1.38-alpha. Serving is cut off by staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/deleted_kinds.go (ResourceExpirationEvaluator), which keys off exactly APILifecycleRemoved — so that tag IS the removal release, and CHANGELOG prose is a secondary source. LESSON: prefer the generated prerelease-lifecycle tags over changelog text for every removedIn in this file; see CatalogGroundTruthTest, which now asserts this mechanically.

newVerifiedRows.quote: Coordination.v1alpha1 API is dropped and replaced with coordination.v1alpha2. Old coordination.v1alpha1 types must be deleted before upgrade
kube-apiserver: Inactive serving code is removed for authentication.k8s.io/v1alpha1 APIs

Introduced scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha2 Workload and PodGroup API to allow for expressing workload-level scheduling requirements and let kube-scheduler act on those. Removed scheduling.k8s.io/v1alpha1 Workload API.
Promotes the scheduling.k8s.io API group from v1alpha2 to v1alpha3 and drops v1alpha2 entirely. Remember to remove all v1alpha2 objects from the api-server while performing the cluster update.
Promoted SnapshotMetadataService to v1beta1. Removed support for the v1alpha1 version.
newVerifiedRows.groupNote: Confirmed via PR file diff that the CRD group is cbt.storage.k8s.io, not storage.k8s.io — this CRD ships from the out-of-tree kubernetes-csi/external-snapshot-metadata sidecar project (test manifest vendored into kubernetes/kubernetes for e2e only), so detection depends on the CRD being installed in-cluster.

newVerifiedRows.quote: Kubeadm: removed the v1beta3 API which was deprecated since v1.31. The 1.35 kubeadm binary can be used to migrate to v1beta4 by using the command 'kubeadm config migrate'.
newVerifiedRows.placement: detectorTable ONLY (not catalogRules) — kubeadm ClusterConfiguration/InitConfiguration/JoinConfiguration are client-side config documents (embedded as YAML text inside the kube-system kubeadm-config ConfigMap, or standalone bootstrap files), never a live top-level Kind scanned by the Tier-A resource inventory, and kube-apiserver never serves or reports metrics for this group. It fits ONLY the pre-apply CrossGuard raw-manifest scan (DeprecatedApiDetector), which is why ResourceKindMap is intentionally NOT updated for these kinds.

advisoryOutOfScope.verdict: OUT OF SCOPE for RemovedVolumePluginCatalog — does NOT map to a detectable Pod-spec field.
advisoryOutOfScope.quote: ACTION REQUIRED: Removed the integrated support for flex-volumes in kubeadm. Users were advised to migrate away from flex-volumes as recommended by SIG Storage since v1.22. If kubeadm users wish to continue using the feature, they need a custom image for the KCM that is not based on distroless, pass the KCM flag --flex-volume-plugin-dir, and mount the directory /usr/libexec/kubernetes/kubelet-plugins/volume/exec in the KCM static pod using kubeadm's extraVolumes mechanism before upgrading to v1.36.
advisoryOutOfScope.reasoning: This is kubeadm's own convenience automation for wiring the kube-controller-manager's --flex-volume-plugin-dir flag + hostPath mount into its static pod manifest at cluster-bootstrap time — NOT the removal of the generic `flexVolume` Pod-spec volume source key itself (the quote's own remediation path — mount the directory yourself via extraVolumes — confirms the underlying flex-volume kubelet mechanism still functions). RemovedVolumePluginCatalog's detection model is 'flag volumeSourceKey presence in a live workload spec'; there is no such workload-spec field affected here, so forcing a row in would produce a structurally meaningless / never-firing rule. Surfaced here as advisory documentation instead, per the task's explicit instruction not to force it.
